title: Checkpoint: Classes and Objects
intro: Check that you can define classes, work with instance and class attributes, use properties, and write special methods.

questions.question: What does this code print?
questions.code:
class Student:
    count = 0

    def __init__(self, name):
        self.name = name
        self.count += 1

a = Student("Aziza")
b = Student("Bekzod")
print(Student.count, a.count)
questions.explanation: self.count += 1 creates an instance attribute on each object and leaves Student.count at 0. Use Student.count += 1.

questions.question: A Product class has a property named price. Inside the class, where should the value itself be stored?
questions.explanation: Assigning to self.price inside the property calls the setter again and again, causing RecursionError. Store the data under another name like self._price.

Prints True, then a set with two products
questions.explanation: The names match, so == is True. Defining __eq__ sets __hash__ to None, so the object cannot go in a set.
